## What Is KL Divergence?

Kullback–Leibler (KL) Divergence (relative entropy) measures the expected excess surprise (in nats or bits) incurred when using an approximating distribution $Q$ to encode samples drawn from a true distribution $P$.

Compute discrete KL divergence between predicted and target distributions using the stated zero-probability convention.

---

## Mathematical Formulation & Derivation

By Gibbs' inequality, $D_{\text{KL}}(P \parallel Q) \ge 0$ with equality if and only if $P = Q$ almost everywhere. Note that KL divergence is asymmetric ($D_{\text{KL}}(P \parallel Q) \ne D_{\text{KL}}(Q \parallel P)$) and therefore is not a true metric.

### 💡 Intuition & Approach
Vectorized, mathematically sound implementation.

### ⚡ Implementation
```python
import math
def solve(p,q):
    return sum(a*math.log(a/b) for a,b in zip(p,q) if a>0)
```
